hook: My $40 ornament box still looked bare. Here's why.

scenes.visual_prompt: Overhead shot of an open 40-piece ornament box next to a 7.5-foot tree
scenes.voiceover: I bought a 40-piece ornament box thinking that would be plenty.

scenes.visual_prompt: Graphic overlay counting branch tips on the tree, number ticking up to 500+
scenes.voiceover: Turns out a 7.5-foot tree has over 500 branch tips. 40 ornaments spread across that reads as empty no matter how evenly you hang them.

scenes.visual_prompt: Side-by-side comparison: ornaments hung one at a time vs. ornaments wired into clusters of three
scenes.on_screen_text: It's a volume problem, not a taste problem
scenes.voiceover: It's not that the ornaments are ugly. It's that there aren't enough of them, and there's no mid-layer between the lights and the ornaments.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand unspooling a velvet ribbon bundle, measuring tape showing 27 feet laid out
scenes.on_screen_text: The fix: 27 ft of velvet ribbon
scenes.voiceover: A $34 bundle ships with about 27 feet of ribbon — that's the standard length for a 3-to-4-wrap spiral on a tree this size.

scenes.visual_prompt: Ribbon being wrapped diagonally, filling the visible gaps between ornament clusters
scenes.on_screen_text: Ribbon fills the gaps the eye catches
scenes.voiceover: The eye picks up negative space between ornaments faster than it picks up color. Ribbon fills exactly that space.

scenes.visual_prompt: Finished tree, full and layered, camera slowly zooms out
scenes.voiceover: Same ornaments I already owned. I just added the ribbon and clustered them instead of hanging them one at a time.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card with blog URL style graphic
scenes.voiceover: Full math is on the blog, link in bio.

caption: If your tree looks sparse, it's not your ornaments' fault. I did the actual branch-tip math on why a 40-piece box can't fill a 7.5-foot tree, and what a $34 ribbon bundle fixes that more ornaments wouldn't.
